facts.statement: Quilmesaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian stages) in the Allen Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Quilmesaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian stages) Allen Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus is classified as a member of the theropod family Abelisauridae, closely related to Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: It was a member of Abelisauridae, closely related to genera such as Carnotaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Quilmesaurus was named and described by Rodolfo Aníbal Coria in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001, Rodolfo Aníbal Coria named and described the type species Quilmesaurus curriei.

facts.statement: The genus name Quilmesaurus honors the Quilmes Native American people, while the species name curriei honors Canadian paleontologist Dr. Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Quilmes, a Native American people, and the specific name honours Dr. Philip John Currie, a Canadian theropod specialist.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Quilmesaurus, designated MPCA-PV-100, is housed in the Museo Provincial "Carlos Ameghino".
facts.quote: The holotype and currently only specimen was designated the collection number MPCA-PV-100, in the Museo Provincial "Carlos Ameghino".

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the distal half of a right femur and a complete right tibia collected from the Allen Formation in the Neuquén Basin.
facts.quote: It consists of the distal (lower or outermost) half of the right femur (thighbone), and a complete right tibia (inner shinbone), collected from the Allen Formation of the Malargüe Group in the Neuquén Basin.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in fluvial sandstones at the base of the Allen Formation, dating from the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: These deposits date from the Campanian to Maastrichtian. The specimen came from the fluvial sandstones at the bottom of the Allen Formation.

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus is notable for representing one of the youngest known non-avian theropod records from Patagonia.
facts.quote: The taxon is notable as it represents one of the youngest records of a non-avian theropod from Patagonia.

facts.statement: In 2016, Quilmesaurus was estimated to be 5.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 2016, Quilmesaurus was estimated to have measured 5.3 m in length.

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus was among the smallest derived abelisaurids, yet it possessed legs that were proportionally robust like those of the large genus Pycnonemosaurus.
facts.quote: This would have made it among the smallest derived abelisaurids, although its legs were proportionally robust like those of Pycnonemosaurus, one of the largest members of the family.

facts.statement: Valieri et al. (2007) concluded that Quilmesaurus is a nomen vanum (dubious name) because no single unique trait could be established for the taxon.
facts.quote: Valieri et al. (2007) were unable to establish a single autapomorphy (distinctive or unique trait) of the taxon, concluding that Quilmesaurus were a nomen vanum.

facts.statement: The validity of the subfamily Carnotaurinae is debated, with some studies including taxa like Majungasaurus and Carnotaurus while others exclude them.
facts.quote: However, the validity of Carnotaurinae has been debated. Although Valieri et al. (2007) considered the subfamily to include taxa such as Majungasaurus, Carnotaurus, Aucasaurus, and Rajasaurus, other studies have found different results.

facts.statement: Filippi et al. (2016) placed Quilmesaurus within the newly defined clade Furileusauria, which groups abelisaurids closer to Carnotaurus than to Ilokelesia, Skorpiovenator, or Majungasaurus.
facts.quote: Filippi et al. (2016) created a new clade, Furileusauria, to include abelisaurids more closely related to Carnotaurus than to Ilokelesia, Skorpiovenator, or Majungasaurus. They included Quilmesaurus among the furileusaurians.

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 75 millones de años durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus lived in what is now South America.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: Remains of Quilmesaurus were found in the Allen Formation, Malargüe Group, Neuquén Basin, at Salitral Ojo de Agua, 40 km south of General Roca, Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron hallados en la Formación Allen, Grupo Malargüe, en la Cuenca Neuquina, en la localidad Salitral Ojo de Agua, 40 kilómetros al sur de la Ciudad de General Roca, Provincia del Río Negro en Argentina

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus was formally described in 2001 by Rodolfo Coria.
facts.quote: Recién fue descrito en 2001 por Rodolfo Coria

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Quilmes indigenous people of northern Argentina, and the species name honors Canadian paleontologist Dr. Phillip J. Currie.
facts.quote: Su nombre proviene de los nativos americanos Quilmes del norte de Argentina y la especie en honor al Dr. Phillip J. Currie, un paleontólogo canadiense especialista en terópodos

facts.statement: Quilmesaurus measured approximately 4.6 meters in length and weighed about 430 kg.
facts.quote: Medía 4,6 m de largo y pesaba 430 kg aproximadamente

facts.statement: A 2016 estimate suggested Quilmesaurus measured 5.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: En 2016, se estimó que Quilmesaurus medía 5,3 metros de longitud

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPCA-PV-100 consists of a complete distal portion of the right femur and tibia from a subadult individual.
facts.quote: El holotipo MPCA-PV-100 consta de una porción distal completa de un fémur y tibia derechos de un ejemplar subadulto

facts.statement: The preserved portion of the femur has a highly developed mid-distal crest with a quadrangular morphology in anterior view.
facts.quote: La porción preservada del fémur tiene una cresta medio-distal altamente desarrollada con una morfología cuadrangular en vista anterior

facts.statement: The cnemial crest is highly developed and expanded at the distal level of the tibia.
facts.quote: La cresta cnemial está altamente desarrollada y expandida a nivel distal

facts.statement: An additional finger-like bony spur, an epicondyle, would have been present on the lateral condyle, though this spur is broken in the only known Quilmesaurus femur.

facts.statement: The distal part of the tibia has projections for connecting to ankle bones, known as malleoli.
facts.quote: La parte distal de la tibia posee sus propias proyecciones para conectarse a los huesos del tobillo, conocidas como maléolos

facts.statement: The only known remains of this genus are leg bones that share certain similarities with a variety of abelisaurids.
facts.quote: Los únicos restos conocidos de este género son los huesos de las piernas que comparten ciertas similitudes con una variedad de abelisáuridos

facts.statement: However, these bones lack unique characteristics, which may make Quilmesaurus a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos huesos carecen de características únicas, lo que puede hacer que Quilmesaurus sea un nomen dubium

facts.quote: Aunque Coria en 2001 consideró que una cresta cnemial en forma de gancho es exclusiva de Quilmesaurus, Valieri et al. en 2007 notaron que esta estructura también la poseían Aucasaurus y Majungasaurus, así como el ambiguo abelisáurido Genusaurus

facts.statement: The Allen Formation is notable for the large quantity of sauropod eggs discovered there.
